questions.q: What is Neo4j Aura, and what edition does it run on under the hood?
options: Neo4j's official fully-managed database-as-a-service, built on Neo4j Enterprise Edition
A third-party hosting provider unaffiliated with Neo4j
A stripped-down version of Neo4j Community Edition with fewer features
A desktop application for running Neo4j locally
questions.explain: Aura is Neo4j's own managed service, and every paid tier runs on Enterprise Edition, giving customers Enterprise-only capabilities without managing licensing directly.

questions.q: Which real Aura tier is described as permanently free, aimed at learning and prototypes?
options: AuraDB Free
AuraDB Business Critical
AuraDS
AuraDB Enterprise Unlimited
questions.explain: AuraDB Free is the small, permanently free single-instance tier; Professional and Business Critical are the paid production tiers, and AuraDS targets graph data science workloads.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a client actually give up by choosing Aura over self-hosting Neo4j Enterprise Edition?
options: Direct infrastructure control — not database capability, since the query language and driver APIs are identical
Access to causal clustering and online backup entirely
The ability to use Cypher as the query language
Nothing at all — Aura and self-hosted Enterprise are functionally identical in every respect including infrastructure access
questions.explain: Aura customers can't SSH into the underlying box or hand-tune OS-level settings, but the database itself — Cypher, drivers, capabilities — is unchanged.

questions.q: Which of the following does Aura take off a DBA's plate, per this lesson?
options: Automatic continuous backups with point-in-time restore, managed clustering and failover, console-driven scaling, and patching
Writing Cypher queries on the client's behalf
Designing the client's graph data model
Aura does not actually manage any of the operational tasks covered elsewhere in this chapter
questions.explain: Aura automates the exact operational work — backup, clustering, scaling, patching, monitoring — that earlier lessons in this chapter taught how to do by hand.

questions.q: How does Neo4j Aura's position in this course compare to MongoDB Atlas and Azure Cosmos DB?
options: It's the same industry pattern repeated — a managed-cloud option sitting next to the self-hosted story, the same way Atlas relates to self-hosted MongoDB and Cosmos DB is managed by definition
Aura is unrelated to Atlas or Cosmos DB and represents a completely different concept
Aura, Atlas, and Cosmos DB are actually the same underlying product rebranded
Only Aura offers a managed option — Atlas and Cosmos DB require full self-hosting
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a repeating industry trend across all three platforms covered in this course.
